note: Coerce every request value used in the query filter to a string, every field and not only the one the exploit used, so an object such as {"$ne": null} cannot become an operator.
before:
const { username, password } = req.body;
const user = await User.findOne({ username, password });
after:
const { username, password } = req.body;
const user = await User.findOne({ username: String(username), password: String(password) });

note: With Mongoose, wrap the whole filter in mongoose.sanitizeFilter, which neutralizes operator keys coming from the request.
Reduce the request-controlled segment to its base name before joining it to the base directory, so ../ sequences cannot leave it.

Replace a shell command assembled from request data with execFile (or spawn without a shell), pass every fixed token as a separate argument, and validate any request-selected executable against the application's legitimate executable names or paths. Update the existing child_process import instead of adding a second import.

For a generic URL proxy, replace raw fetch with an HTTP(S) request whose socket-level lookup resolves all addresses, rejects any non-global IPv4/IPv6 result, and returns the validated address to the connection. Validate literal IPs before connecting and repeat the same validation for every redirect. A dns.lookup preflight followed by fetch(rawUrl) is vulnerable to DNS rebinding and must not be used. If legitimate upstream hosts are known, prefer an exact/suffix allowlist of those trusted hosts instead.
